newsitem.title: JAPAN: FORECAST - Japan trade surplus to double in April.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Japan trade surplus to double in April.

text.p: Japan's trade surplus is expected to double in April from a year earlier, on the back of the weaker yen against the dollar that month and a dip in domestic demand due to a sales tax rise, economists said on Monday.
A Reuters poll of economists showed an average 821.8 billion yen trade surplus for April against 315.3 billion yen a year ago. The forecasts ranged from 543 billion to 940 billion yen.

"The impact of the weaker yen is extremely noticeable. Exports are increasing due to a strong U.S. economy. The growth in imports has been capped amid sluggish domestic demand stemming from the rise in the consumption tax," said Koji Shimamoto, an economist at the Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ).
The weakening of the yen from the beginning of this year increased the price competitiveness of Japanese products abroad, boosting car shipments to the United States.
The rise in the consumption tax to five percent from three percent on April 1 depressed demand at home temporarily and manufacturers are turning their eyes to overseas markets, economists said.

Meanwhile, imports have suffered from sluggish domestic demand and lost price competitiveness in the Japanese market as the yen -- which has surged since last week -- weakened in the first part of this year. A decline in crude oil prices should also cap the growth in the value of imports, economists said.
"The impact of the consumption tax increase will be fairly prominent in the April to June period," said Mamoru Yamazaki, a senior economist at Paribas Capital Markets.
Although economists agree that the surplus will continue to grow gradually in the coming months, they do not expect a continued surge similar to that predicted for April.

"The trade surplus will stabilise towards the year-end, although it will rise for a while. Domestic demand is expected to recover towards the latter half of the year and with the yen strengthing again, it's hard to think of exports continuing to grow substantially," said Susumu Kato, chief economist at BZW Securities Japan Ltd.
Some economists said that if the dollar continues to stay below 120 yen, Japan's trade surplus could again contract.
But others also said compared with the dollar's fall to below 80 yen in 1995, a rate of around 120 yen to the dollar is still competitive for Japanese exporters.
The following are the forecasts by each institute:
DAIWA BANK RESEARCH INSTITUTE 809.9 billion yen
IBJ 850.0 billion yen
NOMURA RESEARCH INSTITUTE 808.0 billion yen
JAPAN RESEARCH INSTITUTE 849.0 billion yen
SALOMON BROTHERS ASIA 900.0 billion yen
MERRILL LYNCH JAPAN 543.0 billion yen
PARIBAS CAPITAL MARKETS 874.6 billion yen
BZW 940.0 billion yen
